title.value: Countering the Effects of Lead Bias in News Summarization via Multi-Stage Training and Auxiliary Losses
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Countering the Effects of Lead Bias in News Summarization via Multi-Stage Training and Auxiliary Losses

analysis.description: The paper addresses the issue of lead bias in neural extractive summarization systems used in the news domain. It proposes two techniques—using unbiased data and introducing an auxiliary ROUGE-based loss—to help systems better balance the importance of content across different sections of a document, rather than favoring sentences at the beginning. The effectiveness of these techniques is demonstrated using state-of-the-art reinforcement learning-based models on the CNN/Daily Mail dataset.

type.justification: The paper describes experimental methods and results using reinforcement learning systems and the CNN/Daily Mail dataset to test proposed techniques, indicating it's an empirical study.
type.quote: We implement these techniques for two recent reinforcement learning based systems, RNES (Wu and Hu, 2018) and BanditSum (Dong et al., 2018), and evaluate them on the CNN/Daily Mail dataset.

name.justification: The study involves extractive summarization, which is a component of Natural Language Processing, specifically dealing with text.
name.quote: Extractive summarization remains a simple and fast approach to produce summaries which are grammatical and accurately represent the source text.

name.justification: The paper specifically addresses techniques in summarization by improving extractive summarization systems.
name.quote: We demonstrate that recent summarization systems over-exploit the inherent lead bias present in news articles.
